_comment: ROIs normalized [x, y, w, h] over 0..1. Values here are TUNED on the real screenshots in __screenshots (full/left/dual). Verify with: python calibrate.py --image <file>

capture._comment: monitor: 1 = primary, 2 = secondary... (mss numbering, see calibrate.py --monitors). region optional in pixels [x, y, w, h] within the monitor, if Zoom has black bars.

states._comment: Detected state -> vMix input sent to program with Merge. DUAL/TRIPLE deliberately stay on 2 until they have a dedicated input in the preset: they are recognized and logged, but the Zoom feed stays on screen. Candidates for later: DUAL -> 29, TRIPLE -> 30. When you wire them up, change the number here AND add it to managed_inputs.

_managed_comment: Inputs the automation is allowed to command. If the program ends up on an input OUTSIDE this list, it goes hands-off and stops correcting: that's how it avoids fighting the operator. 49 = '3 BRO VERSE L', has no keyboard shortcut in the current template.

rois._comment: metric 'navy' = fraction of pixels matching the card's color (H 100-130, S>=150, V<=110) - dark AND saturated blue, nothing else. s_min=150 excludes a dark blue jacket in a camera shot (S~106, darker than the card but above a low s_min) that used to trigger false BIG_LEFT/LEFT (testdata/none_giacca_navy.png). A previous version also counted bright/desaturated pixels as 'card' to tolerate long verse text, but that let a performer's white/cream outfit or a white set piece get misread as a verse card (testdata/none_performance_bianco.png) - removed once we confirmed pure navy, with today's thresholds, already covers every known case including long verses (see each ROI's _note below).

card_left._note: is there a card on the left?  full=0.56 left=0.79 big_left=0.80 dual=0.80 triple=0.49 dual_verso_lungo=0.68  |  camera=0.15 navy_jacket=0.29 performance(white_outfit)=0.00

col_right._note: narrow strip at the card's right edge: where it ends in LEFT and where it continues in BIG_LEFT.  full=0.52 left=0.08 big_left=0.99 dual=1.00 triple=0.85 dual_verso_lungo=0.62  |  camera=0.34 navy_jacket=0.38

far_right._note: right-hand band: card in full/dual, cameras in left/big_left.  full=0.66 left=0.01 big_left=0.01 dual=0.98 triple=0.51 dual_verso_lungo=0.64  |  camera=0.14 navy_jacket=0.34

low_left._note: the card reaches the bottom on the left: full only.  full=0.95 left=0.00 big_left=0.29 dual=0.00 triple=0.01  |  camera=0.06 navy_jacket=0.00

low_right._note: the card reaches the bottom on the right: full only.  full=1.00 left=0.04 big_left=0.27 dual=0.00 triple=0.00  |  camera=0.05 navy_jacket=0.00

template_gate._comment: Optional. Compares a background-only band against a saved reference (python calibrate.py --save-ref) to rule out a camera being on screen instead of the graphic. The ROIs above are already discriminating enough: only enable this if you see false positives.

detector._rules_comment: Evaluated IN ORDER, the first match wins. If none match -> NONE -> input 2: exiting NONE requires positive evidence, and that's what guarantees the fallback to the Zoom feed once the verse disappears. NOTE: across the 5 measured layouts every rule is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE - each one matches only one rule - so the order is not load-bearing. If you add rules, re-check this with test_detection.py.

rules._note: full-page card: the panel reaches the bottom on both sides AND the main card body is present. card_left is required here too, not just low_left/low_right - a wide congregation/venue shot with blue stage drapery flanking both bottom corners can hit low_left/low_right on its own (card_left=0.0) and get misread as FULL for several seconds, real bug found in the field: testdata/none_venue_wide_nueva_ecija.png (low_left=0.735 low_right=0.944 card_left=0.000). Every real FULL frame has card_left >= 0.49 (see module docstring), so this costs no margin on true cases.
two cards on top + one centered at the bottom
two cards side by side, neither reaches the bottom, the right one is wide
wide card on the left + 3 narrow cameras on the right: the card extends past x=0.635 but doesn't reach the far_right band
card on the left ending before x=0.635, 2 cameras on the right
NOT VERIFIED: no screenshot available yet. Mirrors LEFT. Enable only after checking the numbers with calibrate.py --image right.png

overlays._comment: Independent on/off overlay toggles, separate from the verse-card state machine above: production keeps the lower third on through many segments unrelated to a verse (confirmed still on during a real performance frame, testdata/none_giacca_navy.png). Each is reconciled against its own vMix overlay channel via Merge-style Function=OverlayInputN&Input=<vmix_input>, which TOGGLES that channel - safe here because we always re-read the real state first and only send one toggle when it disagrees, same closed-loop principle as the verse switcher, never a blind command chain. Get more real OFF cases before trusting this as hard as the verse-card thresholds - each probe has had exactly one real false positive found and fixed so far (see each probe's _note).

lis_box._note: sign-language interpreter box, bottom-left: solid light-blue backdrop behind the interpreter. h_min/h_max/s_min alone weren't enough: a lower-third banner variant whose saturated blue corner reaches into this screen position was misread as the box (S~208-234 vs the real backdrop's S~128) - see testdata_overlays/false_positive_lower_third_only.png. s_max fixes it. Also corrected two mislabeled test cases that never actually had the box visible (testdata/left_verso_testo_canzone.png, testdata/none_performance_bianco.png - checked visually, no interpreter box in either). With s_max=190: worst real ON=0.30, worst OFF/false=0.02.

lower_third._note: bottom banner: needs the saturated blue bar AND the white text panel together (min of both fractions), not blue alone. Blue-only was fooled twice more within the same evening: a wide venue shot (stage lighting) and a plain sky background both read plenty of 'saturated blue' with zero banner in frame - see testdata_overlays/venue_wide_shot.png and sky_no_banner.png. A photographed scene is easily one glob of blue; it essentially never has a big flat white panel next to a big flat blue one. A later false positive (testdata_overlays/shouldnt-appear-lt.png, a pale cream song-lyrics caption) still passed 'white' at s<=40 while a dark shadow passed 'blue' - fixed by tightening white to s<=15 (see overlays.py). min(blue,white): worst real ON=0.19, worst OFF/false=0.05.

centered_lower_third._note: location caption over the camera panel, top-left (e.g. 'VILLAMOR, PASAY CITY', 'LAOAG CITY, ILOCOS NORTE') - same white-pill/blue-arc graphic family as lower_third but a different vMix input shown in a different spot, so it needs its own box: at lower_third's own box this caption reads far too low to be confused with it, and vice versa. Same 'banner' metric (min of blue-bar and white-panel fractions, white tightened to s<=15 - see overlays.py). Only ONE real ON example so far (testdata_overlays/centered-lowerthird.png, min=0.28); the closest false reading found is testdata/none_giacca_navy.png, now 0.042 after the s<=15 tightening (was 0.165 at s<=40) - on=0.20 sits above that with real margin, but with a single positive example this is less trustworthy than lower_third's thresholds. Get more real ON/OFF cases before tightening further. By production rule (not a detection ambiguity) it must never be commanded on while lower_third is on - see suppressed_by.

timing._comment: confirm_frames: consecutive agreeing readings before accepting a new state (3 at 8fps = ~375ms). command_cooldown_s: minimum wait between two commands to vMix. resync_warn_after: after how many repeated corrections a warning gets logged.
